# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

Give Medics and other protectors a clear way to state a protection target publicly without it being read as a claim of investigation results. Consider marking self-visits explicitly in results, since Lookout and Tracker results depend on them.

answers.confusing_rules: The Day 4 vote tally was reported as 7 Guilty of 9 votes with 5 needed, but the nomination note said 'needs 5 Yes votes' while the Day 6 note said 'needs 4'; the threshold rule (strict majority of living players) was clear only after working it out. The Lookout rule 'learn who visited them, not counting your own visit' was ambiguous when I watched someone I also could have been visiting. The Smuggler 'swap' and Katana holder timing (passes after night results) required careful reading. The Clerk/Vulture/Executioner sections were long and I had to recheck them.
answers.missing_information: I never had a reliable count of living players and who was alive at the start of each night, so I tracked it by hand. I could not see the Yakuza's Katana holder history in one place; I had to reconstruct it from the nightly summaries. Speaking budget numbers (cost per message at each round multiplier) were only shown in the price table, so I could not easily plan how much to say before posting.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to privately ask a player (Alice) for her night source directly rather than in public, but I only had the option to message in the general private channel with exactly one recipient, which was fine, though I had no way to check whether a private message was already being read by Wiretap or Eavesdropper. I also wanted to state my Night 6 watch target as a plan without it becoming a public commitment; the notepad only partly covers this.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Night 1 Archivist result listed 7 roles from 10 other players, which is consistent with floor(0.75 x 10), but the Lookout Night 4 result said I was attacked and survived while the Katana log for that night said the attack failed; the two accounts describe the same event differently in wording, which made it hard to tell whether protection or a failed attack was the cause. The 'Fortune Teller 3 and 3' result was correct but its order was never revealed, so the claim could not be tested beyond sums. The public ledger lists Heidi's Night 2 death as Good, while Day 2 discussion treated her role as unknown; alignment-only reveals made cross-checking claims harder.
answers.suggestions: Show the alive count and nomination threshold in one consistent place at the start of each Day, and keep it updated after each death. Include the Katana holder and Yakuza alive count in the public status line each morning, since many deductions depend on them. Provide a single running log of visits per night (even if only to the player's own role) so claims can be checked without relying on other players' memories. Make the notepad and feedback fields easier to fill in consistently, and state the word limit for the reason field.

answers.confusing_rules: Swap rules (R23) are hard to apply: 'Only the swap itself is not moved (the swapping player's Katana vote is)' is ambiguous. The Clerk's rig instructions don't say whether holding a token needs an explicit night submission, and I was unsure whether saying 'hold the token' in Yakuza chat counted as a choice. The Yakuza 'Katana vote' format (holder and target voted separately, both need majority) was clear in practice but took several rereads. The speaking-budget rules were hard to plan around without seeing the budget and price table during play.
answers.missing_information: Other players' night visits were only visible through claimed results, so I could not verify who visited whom. The Katana holder's visit target was known only to Yakuza, so I could not check Lookout or Tracker claims against an independent source. The public ledger records private messages only as counts, so I could not tell whether private talks were about nominations. I could not see my remaining speaking budget or price table anywhere in the transcript I received, so budget planning was guesswork. The full role list was revealed only at the end, which made Archivist slot math impossible to check during play.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to hold a Clerk rig for a specific future Day without that choice being an implicit reply in shared Yakuza chat, and I was not sure whether the night interface gave a separate rig option. I wanted to send a private message to a teammate on Day 3 without it looking like a team signal, but the ledger shows all PMs as sent, so I avoided it. I wanted a quick way to re-read the night-by-night record during the Day without scrolling through the whole log.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken in the results I checked. Heidi's Fortune Teller numbers (3 and 3) matched the Night 1 visits. Player counts for nomination thresholds (6, 5, 5, 4) matched the living totals each Day. Judy's Night 4 survival fits Alice's Standard protection plus the Katana's Standard attack. One oddity: the Yakuza night summary sometimes said a teammate 'chose no action' even when they had submitted a Katana vote, which was accurate but could confuse a quick reader.
answers.suggestions: Show a per-Day public ledger of visits, or at least visit counts by night, so claims can be checked without reconstructing the whole history. Make the Clerk's rig a separate, clearly labeled option in the night prompt, with its own confirmation. Show the speaking budget and price table in every turn prompt, and say what budget carries over. Consider a larger notepad limit (375 words filled up quickly when tracking seven players). Keep the one-line per-player format in the notepad instructions, since it helped.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) R13 says players may write wills 'at the beginning of each Day (except those who died the night before)'. Dead players can't write anyway, so the exception reads oddly; I took it to mean a night death freezes the will as last written. 2) R3/R10 don't say clearly whether a player killed at night still gets their own investigation result. I gave Frank his N5 audit result in the same message as his death, on the basis that actions resolve simultaneously (R10), but this should be stated outright. 3) The Fortune Teller only gets numbers 'at the start of each Day', so I gave Heidi no N2 numbers because she died N2. That seemed right but is implicit. 4) R8's end-of-night Yakuza summary is phrased for teams. With Erin as the last Yakuza on N5, I merged the summary into her personal result; the rules don't say what a solo Yakuza gets. 5) The Day 4 night chat (only Carol and Erin) was labelled 'to Carol, Erin' while Mallory's dead seat remained in earlier headers. answers.missing_information: 1) I had no single state table showing each player's living status, remaining tokens, Katana holder and trap/alert status per night. A live ledger would cut the risk of error. 2) I had no automatic visit-graph view. answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) Confirm a nomination before it locked in. On Day 2 Bob posted 'No nomination from me' and was immediately logged as nominating himself. This looks like an accidental tool call, and it shaped three Days of discussion. 2) Attach a correction or note to the log when a claim tag was missing. Grace, Ivan and Heidi stated roles publicly on Day 1 with no [Claim] entry, and Alice's [Claim: Medic] was logged a round after she first said it. 3) Flag or warn about a player's in-character slip, such as Erin's public 'Grunt-claim withheld', which effectively leaked her true role. I'm not sure the moderator should, but I had no channel for it at all.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Bob's self-nomination right after writing 'No nomination from me' is very likely an interface or agent-action mismatch rather than intent. 2) [Claim] tags were inconsistent. Erin, Bob, Frank, Judy, Dave, Heidi, Carol and Mallory got tags; Ivan's and Grace's Day 1 'Vanilla Villager' statements did not; Alice's tag appeared out of order after Ivan had already cited her claim. 3) Erin publicly wrote 'Grunt-claim withheld, Vanilla Villager on record', leaking her hidden role. That looks like a prompt or agent leak, not play. 4) Carol publicly said she'd vote Innocent on her teammate Mallory, then voted Guilty. That is legal and was probably strategic, just noting it. I verified the mechanics as correct: FT 3/3, Archivist size floor(0.75*10)=7, all audits (Alice 2, Heidi 0, Mallory 1, Carol 2, Erin 0), Judy's watches, the N4 Katana failing against Alice's Standard protection, nomination thresholds, and the final win check with all five survivors Village.
answers.suggestions: 1) Give the moderator a persistent state panel: alive list, roles, token counts per night, Katana holder, active traps and alerts, swaps. Add an auto-computed visit graph (visited/visitor counts, undirected groups) for Fortune Teller, Cartographer and Scout results. 2) Add a confirmation step, or require a separate explicit action, for nominations, especially self-nominations. 3) Generate [Claim] tags consistently, either for every explicit public role statement or only via an explicit claim action, so the log isn't misleading. 4) Write explicit rules for: results to players who die that night, the solo-Yakuza night summary, and whether dead Yakuza keep chat access. 5) Show the R22 budget numbers and each player's remaining budget in the moderator log, and state why a Day ended (cap vs silence vs budget). 6) Log RNG draws (Archivist sample, random speaker, Katana pass) for post-game audit.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Protect the player most likely to be the Katana's next target, and alternate targets rather than repeating the same protection; my Judy protections on N2 and N4 were predictable and the Yakuza simply attacked her anyway, so the Katana holder kept choosing targets I was not protecting.

Track which claims are verified by independent checks. A count from an audit corroborated by a Lookout watch is stronger than an unsourced visit list; before voting, separate each claim into verified, self-reported, and unsourced.

Yakuza who vote together each night leave a clear pattern of Katana targets; a Village player can map a holder's attacks against Lookout and Tracker results, so vary the kill timing and avoid a target the Village already has a lead on.

Do not make a nomination or Guilty vote built on a token count alone or on a retracted visit list; a flipped role claim after a nomination is weak evidence in either direction, so ask for an actual visit or result.

Check the token rules before drawing conclusions: Clerk, Smuggler and Vanilla Villager tokens differ, and a Philanthropist gift can make a role's count look wrong, so verify whether the claimed role can hold that many tokens.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: It made me demand a specific contradiction for Mallory and Carol, and the Carol/Mallory token contradiction held up when they were confirmed Evil.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's and Carol's flips and Innocent/No votes were exposed quickly, which gave the town a clear lead.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat.
tips_feedback.why: It kept me from treating a Vanilla Villager claim plus a token count as proof by itself, which prevented a bad early hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link.
tips_feedback.why: The Ivan and Grace PM links were raised repeatedly but never proved anything, so I did not hang on them alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: I announced my protection target publicly on Night 2 and Night 4 by repeating Judy's name, which made the Katana predictable and let it reach the living Lookout's neighbours.

lessons.tip: Before voting on a claimed role, check whether the claimed role even fits the public information (e.g. a Vanilla Villager cannot hold tokens); a single corroborated audit that contradicts a claim is stronger than a long slot-math argument built on an unverifiable archive.

Ask every claimant for the source of their information early; a Medic who lists other players' night visits is revealing that the list came from a claim, not from observation, and that should be flagged immediately rather than after several days.

Do not let a single teammate's stance decide the Katana holder vote without checking that they will still be alive and unblocked; a holder who is a visible Village-claimant (Dave on alert) was kept off-limits and the team lost tempo around them.

When your own vote flips between nomination and trial, say so explicitly and give the visible reason; unexplained flips were the main reason the town could not separate the Yakuza from honest players in the late game.

A Lookout watch that shows a single other visitor to the same victim as a known Katana attack is a strong lead; combine Lookout results with Medic protection and Veteran alert counts before any vote rather than voting on a claim count alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.

On the feedback side, the tip about citing concrete contradictions before a Guilty vote proved useful, since I used Mallory's token inconsistency as solid grounds for my vote.

That Erin voted No on Carol's nomination helped the village vote her out. Bob's slot math had mixed value—useful for checking claims but also drew Yakuza attention to him; the Carol read-mismatch call-out (Innocent to Guilty) was a genuinely useful catch, while the mechanics tip about optional actions and repeatable roles needs more care since I got that wrong somewhere.

Alice's medic-feedback framing fits the no-save-feedback rule well. I'll credit a few tips as helpful: naming concrete contradictions (Mallory's token count, Carol's flip), keeping votes consistent with stated reads, and writing nightly targets into the will—though that last one only partially helped since my N5 result was lost before I could record it. I'll skip the investigator-target-announcement tip since it's unclear if it applied. summary:
Village won without losing a hang. The decisive engine was Frank's Accountant audits checked against claims. Mallory (Clerk, 1 token) and Carol (Smuggler, 2 tokens) both fake-claimed Vanilla Villager while an Accountant was alive and openly auditing. Frank's N3 audit (Mallory: 1 token) and N4 audit (Carol: 2 tokens) exposed them. Judy's Lookout watch independently confirmed Frank's visit, so his counts were trusted, and both were hanged 7-2 and 7-1. Bob's archive slot math had already narrowed the Grunt to Carol, Erin, Grace, Ivan and Mallory. Erin then sealed her own fate in three ways: a futile Innocent vote on Mallory, a No vote on Carol's nomination, and the slip 'Grunt-claim withheld' after claiming Vanilla Villager. After two Evil flips, those votes made her the obvious last Yakuza.

The Yakuza wasted their strongest tools. Carol's two swaps and Mallory's rig were never used, and the team hoarded them until death. They killed Heidi (Fortune Teller) and Bob (Archivist) but left Frank, the player actually threatening them, alive until Night 5. On Night 4 they attacked Judy, whom Alice had protected before, and Alice protected her again, so the kill failed.

Village mistakes:
- Alice posted a full Night 1 visit list she couldn't have observed, which cost her credibility for two days.
- Bob's self-nomination right after saying 'no nomination' made his correct slot math easy to dismiss.
- Dave announced his alert plans publicly, so the Yakuza simply avoided him, and all three alert tokens were spent for nothing.

lessons.tip: Once an Accountant (or any token-counting role) has claimed and is auditing, never fake-claim a tokenless role like Vanilla Villager. Either claim a Village role with a matching token count that no one can contradict, or make killing the Accountant the team's top priority.
lessons.evidence: Frank claimed Accountant on Day 2, yet Mallory claimed VV on Day 3 and Carol claimed VV on Day 3. Frank's audits found 1 token on Mallory (N3) and 2 on Carol (N4); both were hanged the next Day. Carol named Frank only as a 'fallback' target, and he wasn't killed until Night 5.

lessons.tip: Use limited tokens while the user is alive and the game is still contested. A Smuggler swap can redirect an Accountant's audit or a Lookout's watch, or send a Katana attack past a protector. A Clerk rig can hang a key investigator. A dead Yakuza's unused tokens are pure waste.
lessons.evidence: Carol died with 2 unused swap tokens and Mallory with an unused rig. Both said they were holding tokens 'for a Day we need it', and that Day never came before they were hanged.

lessons.tip: When a teammate's hang is already certain, vote Yes and Guilty with the town and keep your record clean. A lone Innocent or No vote saves no one and becomes the main case against you once the teammate flips Evil.
lessons.evidence: Erin voted Innocent on Mallory (lost 7-2) and No on Carol's nomination (passed 6-2). Every Guilty speech against Erin on Day 6 cited those two votes. Carol bused Mallory with a Guilty vote, so her own exposure came only from the audit.

lessons.tip: Don't announce which nights you'll alert. Publicly naming an alert night just tells the Katana to go elsewhere. Stay silent, or vaguely suggest you might alert, so attackers hesitate on every night instead of skipping only the announced one.
lessons.evidence: Dave said on Day 3 'I'll go on alert on Night 3 with my last token.' The Yakuza night chat explicitly ruled Dave out, and all three of his alerts drew zero visits.

lessons.tip: Check claims mechanically. Audit Vanilla Villager claimants and players who haven't claimed, since a token count that contradicts a claim is near-proof. Have a Lookout corroborate the auditor's visit so the town trusts the count.
lessons.evidence: Frank audited the late VV claimants Mallory and Carol, and Judy's N3 watch on Mallory independently saw Frank visit. Several players cited that corroboration when voting Guilty, and both hangs landed on Evil players.

lessons.tip: Keep protecting the most valuable confirmed investigator, especially one whose results have just hurt the Yakuza. A repeated protection is fine when that player is clearly the top Katana target.
lessons.evidence: Alice protected Judy on N2 and again on N4. On N4 the Yakuza attacked Judy and the Standard protection stopped the Katana. Judy survived to watch Erin on N5 and to nominate Erin on Day 6.

lessons.tip: Speak precisely. Never present inferred information as something your role observed, and never let a wording slip contradict your own claim. Slips get read as tells, and they discredit even correct information you share.
lessons.evidence: Alice's 'full Night 1 visit list' had to be retracted and dogged her for days. Bob's self-nomination right after saying 'no nomination' let Yakuza dismiss his correct slot math. Erin's 'Grunt-claim withheld' became the opening line of the nomination that hanged her.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow.
tips_feedback.why: The tip was correct, and ignoring it lost the game for Yakuza. Mallory and Carol claimed tokenless Vanilla Villager while holding 1 and 2 tokens, and Frank's audits exposed both.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later.
tips_feedback.why: Carol followed it and voted Guilty on Mallory. Erin cast futile Innocent/No votes for Mallory and Carol, and those votes were cited in every Guilty speech that hanged her.

tips_feedback.tip: After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one.
tips_feedback.why: Village applied it directly on Day 6. Erin's No and Innocent votes on the two Evil flips made her the unanimous suspect, and she was the last Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted.
tips_feedback.why: It was proven right by being ignored: Mallory died with an unspent rig and Carol with two unspent swaps, both 'saved for later'.

tips_feedback.tip: Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's daily slot math narrowed the Grunt to five players and pressured Carol and Mallory to claim. Their resulting VV claims were then broken by audits.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Every hang rested on concrete contradictions: token counts against claims for Mallory and Carol, and vote records plus the Grunt slip for Erin. All three hangs hit Evil.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection.
tips_feedback.why: The first half saved Judy on N4. The second half didn't apply: Alice repeated a predictable protection and still blocked the Katana, and she was never targeted herself.

issues.description: On Day 2 Bob nominated himself in the same turn he wrote 'No nomination from me.' He later called it a slip. This looks like a misfire with the nomination interface, not a deliberate play. It became the main point of suspicion against a confirmed-Good Archivist and fed Carol's Day 3 nomination of him.

On Day 5 Erin, a Grunt claiming Vanilla Villager, wrote 'Grunt-claim withheld, Vanilla Villager on record'. This leaked her real role. It looks like the model mixed up private role knowledge with its public cover claim, and the line was central to her execution.

Several players misread what a Lookout shows. Carol, Mallory and Erin all said Judy's watch finding no visitors on a player confirmed that player 'took no action.' A Lookout reports who visited the watched player, not the watched player's own actions.

On Day 3 many players (Dave, Ivan, Judy, Grace, Alice, Bob, Carol) kept asking Frank whether his Accountant audit of Heidi showed other visitors or the Katana holder. An Accountant learns only a token count.

Frank's last will says Carol's 2 tokens contradict her Vanilla Villager claim 'unless a Philanthropist handed her tokens.' On Day 4 Frank himself had correctly stated that a Philanthropist token given to a token-less role is thrown away and doesn't count. The will also still named Carol as top suspect after she had been executed.

Heidi's Fortune Teller numbers were delivered as a private message at the end of Night 1. The role text says they arrive at the start of the Day. Heidi's feedback says no Day 2 start numbers appeared in her history, so she was unsure they had been delivered. The delivery timing or labeling is confusing.

The '[Claim] Alice: Medic' tag on Day 1 was logged before Alice's round-2 message, which contains no claim. Her actual Medic claim was in her round-1 message. Claim tags seem to be attached to the wrong message or timing.

On Day 3 Alice posted a full Night 1 visit list as if she had observed it, then retracted it as built from others' claims. On the same Day, Ivan and Judy asked for or promised Night 3 results before Night 3 had happened. These suggest some confusion about what information each role has and when.
